notes:
Context: Lodestar is building a real-time personalization + fraud-scoring layer for several customer-facing fintech products. Heavy mix of chat (support), reranking for recommendations, and embeddings for fast semantic search.

Key performance asks (from SE + infra):
- Minimum sustained throughput: negotiate guarantee for 45,000 tokens/sec across dedicated pool (sustained for 24h window). They want predictable unit economics not per-request variability.
- Concurrency caps: soft cap at 500 concurrent active streams, hard cap 750 with graceful rejection. Want per-customer concurrency slices so spikes from one product A don't starve product B.
- Burst policy: allow x2 burst for up to 10 minutes per hour (examples: marketing events). Bursts should be billed as overage or drawn from burst credits.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms for first-token for short prompts (<128 tokens), p95 < 350ms for 512-token completions. Need clear definition of measurement window and synthetic vs production traffic.
- Reserved GPU planning: preliminary plan = 32 x A100-80GB equivalent (baseline) with option to expand to 48 during Q4 peak. Seeking guidance from Redwood Optimize on quantization profiles to hit targets with fewer GPUs.
- SLA/credits: they want explicit credits for missed min-tokens/sec (sliding 6h window) and for sustained latency SLO misses. Legal pushed for cap on credits and defined amplification for repeated misses.

POC notes (technical):
- POC ran on Redwood Dedicated trial pool. Observed throughput troughs during KV cache warmup; SE recommended prefix caching + sticky routing.
- Model preference: tuned Llama-class model family (quantized for cost) + fallback to a slightly smaller family when capacity constrained. Lodestar requests automated fallback policy in routing with per-route version pinning.
- Autoscale behavior: Lodestar wants minimal autoscale buffer (1-2 GPUs) to avoid extra cost; concerned about cold-start latency when scaling up.

Procurement/Commercial items: 
- Pricing ask: committed monthly GPU hours with a predictable tokens/unit price. Want example TCO scenarios at 32 vs 48 GPUs.
- Contract term: 24 months preferred. Request inclusion of burst credit pool (e.g., 200M tokens/month) and an overage rate cap.
